newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-AUCKLAND CONFIRM SUPER 12 DOMINATION.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-AUCKLAND CONFIRM SUPER 12 DOMINATION.

text.p: Auckland completed an unbeaten rampage through the ranks of their Super 12 rivals with a 34-20 win against New South Wales in the final round of the regular season on Saturday.
But the Super 12 champions had to dig deep to overcome a fiercer than expected challenge from mid-table New South Wales.
Auckland secured victory by scoring 21 unanswered points in a determined second half display.
But their celebrations were dampened in the final minute when inspirational scrumhalf Ofisa Tonu'u went off with what appeared to be a painful shoulder injury.
Trailing by seven points at halftime, Auckland lifted their game after the interval with two quick tries from winger Brian Lima and second rower Dylan Mika.
All Black lock forward Robin Brooke transformed the match after entering the fray as a substitute in the 53rd minute, stirring the powerful and increasingly dominant Auckland pack.
Lima sealed victory against New South Wales with his second try late on after another period of intense Auckland pressure.
Auckland fullback Adrian Cashmore gave an outstanding kicking display by converting all four tries and adding two penalties.
It was Auckland's 10th win in 11 Super 12 matches this season. Only Northern Transvaal prevented a clean sweep by holding the New Zealanders to a draw in the first round in March.
"We set ourselves a target of remaining unbeaten throughout the regular season and we have achieved that goal. The way we went about the task pleased me a lot," said Auckland captain Zinzan Brooke.
"But it will count for nothing in the semifinal next weekend," said Brooke, who opened his side's scoring after nine minutes with a pushover try from the back of the scrum.
New South Wales briefly seized the initiative just before halftime when winger Alistair Murdoch scored two tries in five minutes to give the home side a 20-13 lead.
Both tries were converted by fullback Matthew Burke, who also kicked two penalties.
